hypotheses.name: raster-projection-identity
hypotheses.statement: The 14 PNGs are the deterministic raster projection of the pitch PDF's 14 pages at 150 dpi; the count and geometry invariants survive.
hypotheses.check: probe.json checks: count_equals_pitch_pages=true, uniform_geometry=true (2000x1125), aspect_16_by_9=true, all_pinned=true.

hypotheses.name: structure-swap
hypotheses.statement: The projection drops the text layer as text: words become pixels and are no longer machine-grep-able, while geometry is preserved exactly (150/72 = 25/12 scale).
hypotheses.check: 959.76 x 540 pts -> 2000 x 1125 px; 540*150/72 = 1125 exact, 959.76*150/72 = 1999.5 -> 2000 (round-up). Words exist in evidence text layer only, not in the PNG bytes as text.

hypotheses.name: carrier-overlap
hypotheses.statement: Pixel weight (PNG bytes) tracks verbal weight (words per page), i.e. the two carriers overlap.
hypotheses.check: pearson(words, bytes) = 0.4648 — only ~46% shared variance; not rejected outright but far from identity.

hypotheses.name: zero-added-meaning
hypotheses.statement: The PNGs add no meaning beyond the pitch PDF itself.
hypotheses.check: Rejected: the pixel layer carries the visual grammar the text layer dropped. slide-14 (thesis page) = 27 words / 234 KB = 8.66 KB/word; slide-09 (value matrix) = 68 words / 204 KB = 3.0 KB/word. The thesis is carried visually 2.9x heavier per word than the matrix — information present in pixels, absent in text.

hypotheses.name: pixel-text-equivalence-via-ocr
hypotheses.statement: OCR of the PNGs would reproduce the evidence text layer page-for-page.
hypotheses.check: Not executed: no OCR engine installed on this machine. The pixel layer's typography/color/layout semantics are not machine-read; only size-distribution proxies were measured.
